task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of July 15, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer using a municipal roof contract to answer why an approved construction invoice can still leave a contractor waiting for part of its money.

facts.text: Wickmere Roofing installed the main roof under a $200,000 contract at the Loden municipal workshop in June 2026.
The city certified the package's invoice but withheld 5%, or $10,000, under the contract's retention provision.
Wickmere received $190,000 rather than the full certified amount.
The written provision releases half the retained amount after completion inspection and the rest after a six-month defect-correction period, subject to its stated conditions.
The provision is part of this contract, not a claim that all construction contracts use the same percentage or release dates.
The city inspector identified an unfinished gutter connection that must be completed before the first $5,000 release.
Wickmere accepts that the connection remains unfinished and says the specified fitting is on order.
The city has budgeted the retained money and says the withholding is not caused by an empty project bank account.
Contractor owner Edda Marsh says suppliers and workers were paid on shorter schedules than the final contract releases.
The firm has five employees, whose combined regular gross payroll is approximately $4,800 a week.
The retained amount is more than two such weekly payrolls, but it is not necessarily the firm's profit on the roof package.
Marsh has not disclosed the package's full material, labor and overhead costs.
Marsh said, "The work can be on the building while part of the payment is still on somebody else's calendar."
City contracts manager Iri Keld says the retained payment gives Wickmere a financial incentive to finish the incomplete details.
Keld said, "Certification records the work's value. Release of the last money has another set of checks."
The city says it will inspect promptly after the fitting is installed but has not set a date because delivery remains uncertain.
The six-month period does not begin merely because the original invoice was submitted; the contract ties it to the defined completion stage.
Wickmere has asked future public clients whether smaller packages can use a lower retention percentage.
The municipal workshop houses road-maintenance equipment, and other contractors handled its electrical and door work under separate contracts.
The record contains no finding that either party breached this contract and no announced change to citywide procurement rules.

forbidden_additions: The city cannot afford payment or the entire invoice is unpaid
An automatic release date, a universal retention rule or $10,000 established as contractor profit
